prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: for the orders placed from 3 to 16 March 2025 (order_ts holds UTC time: use its UTC date), which promotion was each order line sold with? Return two columns, in this order: order_line_id and promo_code. Return one row for each of those order lines whose promotion is in promotions; leave out lines with no promotion. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check the ON of the join to promotions: which column of the line names its promotion?
The query matches promotions to the line's product ID, so the codes belong to unrelated promotions; the line has its own column for the promotion it was sold with.
starter_sql:
SELECT ol.order_line_id, pr.promo_code
FROM order_lines ol
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
JOIN promotions pr ON pr.promo_id = ol.product_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-03' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-17'
why_this_works: Each order line carries the promo_id it was sold with, so joining promotions on that column gives each line its own promotion.
